name: Pay system for 290,000 employees
note: What a pay system actually is: Employee × Rate × Hours = Deposit. Shopify processes billions. Tim Hortons pays 15 people on time for $30/month. A CS student could build one in a weekend.

name: ArriveCAN — a COVID questionnaire app
note: What it actually is: a web form with 10 fields and a QR code. A competent developer builds this in 3 days. 76% of subcontractors did zero work.

name: Long Gun Registry — a database
note: What it actually is: a table with columns (Name, Address, Serial Number, Type). Your local library catalogue is more complex. Original budget: $2 million.

name: Hunting 84 deer on a BC island
note: That's $9,524 per deer. With helicopters and semi-automatic weapons. Any hunter in Canada would have done it for a tag and a case of beer.

name: Catching one (1) bullfrog
note: Parks Canada. Four years. One bullfrog. A 12-year-old with a net would have done it for free.

name: Flying a Canadian chef to India to cook Indian food
note: India. Home of Indian food. They flew a Canadian there to make it. During a state visit. With your money.

name: 86 leather chair cushions (Mexico City embassy)
note: $286 per cushion. You can get a whole leather chair at Costco for less.

name: A fence at Signal Hill, Newfoundland
note: Put up. Taken down one week later. $65,000 for a fence that existed for 7 days. That's $9,286 per day of fence.

name: A barn at Rideau Hall
note: Eight million dollars. For a barn. Your tax dollars built the most expensive barn in Canadian history. The cows must be thrilled.

name: EV battery subsidies to foreign multinationals
note: $28.2 billion to Stellantis, VW, and Northvolt (bankrupt). 20-year break-even "hope." Stellantis responded with layoffs. You paid for that.

name: Trans Mountain Pipeline (original est. $5.4B)
note: 6x over budget. Up to $18.8 billion in projected taxpayer losses. $1,255 per Canadian household. But there's no money for veterans.
